Subject: Dedicated capacity - autoscaling, queue sizing & routing (post-call recap)

Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we heard from your infra and ML teams: 

1) Workload summary (what you told us)
- Primary use: contextual search + reranking for knowledge base and support synthesis.
- Expected steady-state: ~40 QPS, peak bursts up to 200 QPS during product launches.
- Typical request: 1.5k tokens input + 150 tokens output (~1650 tokens total) for generative synthesis; embeddings calls much smaller (~256 tokens).
- SLA target: p99 latency < 250ms for rerank/embedding paths; sampling/generation can be 800–1200ms p95.

2) Key integration items we discussed
- SDK & auth: plan to use Redwood SDK with API key auth for initial integration; AtlasML expressed interest in mTLS for Private later.
- Routing: route low-latency rerank/embedding requests to Dedicated capacity pool with pinned model variant; fall back to hosted API in cross-region outage.
- Structured output/tool calling: will use Redwood structured-output hints + tool-calling interface for connector orchestration.
- Embeddings/rerankers: keep embeddings in your vector DB (we recommend prefix caching and batched embed calls).

3) Dedicated capacity sizing & autoscaling guidance (high level)
- GPU pool recommendation: start with 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (NVIDIA A10x2 or similar) to support steady 40 QPS with headroom for 2x burst.
- Concurrency & batching: aim for per-GPU active concurrency of 8–12 streams for autoregressive sampling; increase batch window to 40–80ms for higher GPU utilization while preserving p95 latency targets.
- Queueing: implement a short in-memory request queue with token-based priority for embeddings and rerankers (max queue depth ~300 requests; soft drops after 800ms wait).
- Autoscaling policy: scale by measured GPU utilization + queue depth. Trigger add when GPU util > 70% OR queued requests > 150 for >30s. Scale down when util < 40% and queue empty for 120s.

4) Next steps / asks for your team
- Please review the attached sizing spreadsheet (dedicated_capacity_sizing.xlsx) and add actual RPS/tokens per req by endpoint.
- Share expected concurrency per user/session and any hard p99 SLAs.
- Tech deep-dive: propose Thu 10/31 10am PT for an infra deep-dive to validate autoscale thresholds and auth options.

Attaching a quick flow diagram (redwood_dedicated_flow.png) and sizing sheet. I pulled conservative numbers to start — happy to iterate after your inputs.

Thanks,

Aditya — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple of clarifying items from our infra side after reviewing the sheet: 

1) Token counts: the 1.5k/150 estimate is correct for synthesis, but rerank pipeline is often 12 candidates * ~512 tokens each — so peak token amplification can be large. We'll add better per-endpoint numbers to the sheet.

2) Concurrency: our app layer maintains ~300 concurrent sessions during peak, but only ~60 active requests/sec to the model layer today. We're evaluating whether to multiplex multiple sessions into single model requests for cost. Thoughts?

3) Auth & network: initial plan is API keys over private network (VPC peering). Long term we'd require mTLS + per-request signed tokens for audit. For Private deployment we'd need HSM/KMS integration.

4) Question on fallback: if Dedicated pool is saturated and we fall back to Hosted, do you preserve request routing for sensitive data? We need to confirm data residency policies.

We filled a few baseline numbers in the sizing tab; will add the detailed rerank token counts tomorrow. Thu 10/31 10am PT works for the deep-dive — adding Priya (Eng Manager) to this thread.

—Sam

Sam / Priya — great notes. Quick answers and a couple of updated recommendations given the rerank amplification: 

- Multiplexing: if you can batch multiple candidate scoring requests into a single model call (i.e., concatenated contexts with separators) you can drastically reduce per-token overhead and improve batching. Our SDK supports grouped requests and will maintain per-request correlation IDs so you can un-bundle results.

- Rerank amplification & GPU sizing: with 12x candidates at 512 tokens each, effective token load per logical request can be ~6k tokens. For that pattern I’d recommend increasing the initial pool to 12 GPUs OR adding larger instance types (e.g., 2x faster GPUs) to keep headroom for bursts while keeping p99s under 300ms for rerank.

- Queueing & priority: implement a two-queue approach — high-priority (rerank/embeddings) and best-effort (long-gen). High-priority queue should preempt and reserve 25% of GPU capacity. This avoids long-gen tasks from starving interactive rerank requests.

- Autoscale tuning specifics (proposals to put in the spreadsheet):
  * Scale-up policy: add 2 GPUs when (avg GPU util > 70% AND queued high-priority > 50) OR queued total > 200 for 45s.
  * Scale-down policy: remove 1 GPU when (avg GPU util < 45% AND queued total < 50 for 3 consecutive 60s windows).
  * Cooldown: 180s to avoid oscillation.

- Auth/routing/fallback: fallback to Hosted will only be used for non-sensitive workloads by default. For customers requiring strict data residency (you), we support policy-based routing: mark endpoints as "do_not_fallback" and Redwood will return 429s when Dedicated is unavailable instead of routing to Hosted. For Private deployments we can enable mTLS + per-request signatures and integrate with your KMS/HSM.

I updated the sizing sheet with a "rerank amplification" column and two GPU pool scenarios (8-GPU conservative, 12-GPU recommended for heavy rerank). Attaching updated spreadsheet.

Next steps:

- We'll run a short cost/headroom calc and share a recommended Dedicated commitment for 3-month and 12-month options.
- Tech deep-dive Thu 10/31 10am PT (we'll send a calendar invite).

Thanks,
